children: GE Aerospace

signed a preliminary agreement with Poland’s Military Aviation Works to explore establishing domestic maintenance and repair capabilities for the engines powering the Polish Air Force’s fleet of KAI FA-50 fighter jets.
The memorandum of understanding covers potential maintenance, repair and overhaul services, including depot-level maintenance, for the F404-GE-102 engine. GE Aerospace
and Military Aviation Works, known locally as WZL-2, will assess the equipment, facilities and other requirements needed to service the engines in Poland.

image.alt: GE Aerospace’s presence in Poland spans over 30 years

children: The Polish Air Force ordered 48 FA-50 light combat aircraft in 2022. The first 12 jets, delivered in 2023, use the FA-50GF “Gap Filler” configuration. An additional 36 aircraft are expected in the more advanced FA-50PL configuration.
The proposed arrangement would cover the engines for all 48 aircraft, along with spare engines.
For investors, the agreement could expand GE Aerospace’s

long-term defense aftermarket business in Europe. Engine maintenance and spare-parts services can generate recurring revenue well after the initial delivery of an aircraft. However, the memorandum is exploratory, and GE Aerospace
did not disclose potential revenue, investment requirements or a timetable for reaching a definitive agreement.
Building maintenance capacity in Poland
GE Aerospace

said establishing local support would help improve aircraft readiness and availability for the Polish military. WZL-2 also described domestic maintenance capacity as a way to strengthen Poland’s operational independence and reduce its reliance on overseas service providers.

The agreement comes as Poland increases defense spending and expands its military capabilities in response to heightened security concerns in Europe. Developing a domestic support network could make the FA-50 fleet easier and potentially less expensive to maintain over its operating life.

WZL-2 is part of Polska Grupa Zbrojeniowa, Poland’s state-controlled defense group. The company provides maintenance and modernization services for military aircraft and engines while expanding into civil aviation and unmanned aircraft systems.
Large installed base for aftermarket
GE Aerospace

has delivered more than 4,000 F404 engines, which have accumulated over 13 million flight hours. About 300 of the engines power the T-50, TA-50 and FA-50 aircraft produced by Korea Aerospace Industries.
That installed base supports demand for inspections, replacement components, repairs and engine overhauls. Establishing additional regional maintenance capacity could help GE Aerospace
capture more of that aftermarket activity while supporting international sales of F404-powered aircraft.

The company has operated in Poland for more than 30 years and employs more than 2,300 people across five locations. The proposed partnership would deepen its presence in the country, although the companies must still complete their assessment before committing to a Polish maintenance facility.
